head: claude/ib-stop-price-reconciler
title: PROPOSAL (Tier-3, draft): reconcile a resting IB protective leg whose PRICE diverges from the journal
body:
**Tier-3 PROPOSAL — draft, awaiting explicit operator approval. No code changes; nothing here has run against a broker.**

This is the "analyse and propose the exact change" half the permission tiers require for the live order path (`src/runtime/order_monitor.py`, `src/units/accounts/ib_client.py`). One new doc, no `src/`, no `config/`, no VM.

## The gap

`IBClient.protection_coverage` has been corrected twice — boolean→quantity (`BL-20260814`), one-sided→two-sided (`BL-20260816`) — and **it still cannot see PRICE**. `legs` is an integer COUNT, not a list; there is no price in the verdict and none in any consumer (`auxPrice` appears in `src/` exactly once, in the dump surface; `aux_price`/`lmt_price` appear in `scripts/` zero times).

So the sweep asks *"how much qty rests?"* and can never ask *"at what price?"*

## Measured (`ib_paper`, 2026-08-20T22:26:01Z, `read_state: orders_read`)

| sym | trade | pos | declared SL | resting STP | Δ |
|---|---|--:|---|---|---|
| MHG | 4796 | 29 | 6.221714 | 6.2215 | ✓ |
| MGC | 4773 | 95 | 4371.1469 | 4371.1 | ✓ |
| MES | 4350 | 15 | 7533.696429 | **7516.50** | **69 ticks** |

**MES is protected 17.196 points below its declared stop — $1,289.73 on 15 contracts.** It graded FULLY STOP-COVERED: quantity right, side right, only the price wrong. MHG and MGC match within a tick in the same read, so this is an outlier, not rounding.

It is a **direct consequence of the over-cover remediation**: `BL-20260816` records order 375 @ 7533.75 (matches the journal) and 338 @ 7516.5 (does not). 375 was cancelled and 338 kept — the leg that matched the journal is the one removed, which is what that row's own criterion #1 exists to prevent.

## ⚠️ This PR corrects an error I made earlier today

I told the operator that `place_protective` "only places, never cancels", and therefore that **no safe one-shot repair existed**. That is **wrong**. `_locked_place_protective` **pre-cancels the symbol's resting protective legs before arming** (OCA-group-scoped when given, symbol-wide otherwise — `BL-20260624-MHG-FLIP`), and `modify_protective` delegates to it precisely to avoid a double-cancel.

That correction is what makes the proposal small, and it rules out the two repairs I had been weighing:

- **`cancel_ib_order --force-protective --force-client-id`** — order 338 is owned by **clientId 497, the trader's own execution band**. That tool refuses `< 9000` by default *because connecting as it evicts the trader's live IB session*; it also leaves the position naked for up to 300 s.
- **place-then-cancel** — two 15-lot stops in **disjoint OCA groups**, i.e. exactly the double-fire → naked-short hazard `BL-20260816` is about.

The correct repair is **one `modify_protective` call on the trader's own client**, carrying the journal's declared levels: cancel-and-re-arm as one operation, no eviction, no disjoint window.

## The proposal

- **`protection_coverage`** additively emits `stop_prices` / `target_prices` / `unpriced_legs` — prices it is already iterating. No existing consumer changes. Stop-family classification keeps testing FIRST (`"STP LMT"` contains `"LMT"`; an LMT-first test would *manufacture* target coverage).
- **The existing `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` sweep** grades `aligned` / `diverged` / **`ungradeable`** against `trades.stop_loss` — read, never invented. **No new broker round-trip**; the account-wide read is already paid for.
- **`ungradeable` is never folded into `aligned`.** That fold is the exact bug class this accessor has now paid for three times.
- **Repair gated by `IB_PROTECTIVE_PRICE_MODE`** (`annotate` default / `apply`) — a `*_MODE` var following the `NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE` precedent, not a default-off `*_ENABLED` flag. `apply` passes **both** journal legs, because the re-arm rebuilds the whole OCA pair and sending one would drop the other.

Six tests are specified that fail without the fix, including **MHG as the discriminating control** — a grader that flags all three is as broken as one that flags none.

## What I have NOT verified, stated up front

- **No code here has been run.** The diff is read off the current files.
- **The tolerance is unchosen.** One tick is a starting point, not a measured value — n=3 on one account on one day. Shipping a threshold on that would be the exposure-ceiling mistake; `annotate` mode exists to produce the distribution first.
- **`BL-20260816-IB-PROTECTIVE-STOPS-NEVER-SET-OUTSIDERTH` is untouched and interacts with this** — a re-arm through this path inherits whatever `outsideRth=False` means for a GTC futures stop, which this repo holds no evidence on.

There is **no urgency**: MES sits ~131 points above the resting stop on a paper account. That is the argument for doing this properly rather than firing a one-off tonight.
